subject.title: fix(acp): ACP session startup fails when backend does not advertise thinking config

question: How should existing ACP session rows containing thinking but no provenance be classified during upgrade?
rationale: Those rows cannot reveal whether thinking was explicit or inherited; default classification may silently discard explicit intent, while strict classification preserves intent but can leave existing affected sessions unable to resume without recovery action.

options.title: Keep legacy rows strict
options.body: Treat missing provenance as explicit or unknown, persist provenance for new writes, and provide a clear reset or Doctor recovery path for affected legacy sessions.

options.title: Treat legacy rows as defaults
options.body: Classify missing provenance as inherited so existing limited-backend sessions recover automatically, accepting that old explicit thinking may be skipped.

options.title: Pause for an inferable migration
options.body: Do not land the stored-data change until another durable source can distinguish legacy explicit requests from inherited defaults.

recommendation.title: Keep legacy rows strict
recommendation.body: Treat missing provenance as explicit or unknown, persist provenance for new writes, and provide a clear reset or Doctor recovery path for affected legacy sessions.
